messages:
maria-ux: heads up — hitting a socket buildup when cancelling Retrofit calls on API 30 with HTTP/2. Repro in attached sample app: keep sending requests, cancel on rotation, sockets pile up. cc @devin-sdk @samir-android

devin-sdk: ugh. any logs or a minimal repro? last time this sounded like dispatcher/connectionpool args.

samir-android: minimal repro steps i used on Pixel 3 emulator (API 30): 1) start continuous polling request every 200ms 2) rotate device / trigger config change to cancel inflight calls 3) observe sockets with `ss -nat | grep TIME_WAIT` increasing and `lsof -p <app_pid>` shows okio threads still holding fds

samir-android: log snippet (trimmed):
```
I/OkHttp: --> GET /v1/embeddings (cancelled)
I/OkHttp: <-- HTTP/2 200 server push
W/OkHttp: call canceled
E/Network: Failed to close socket: Socket closed
```

samir-android: important detail: we use an Authenticator that synchronously does a token refresh inside `authenticate()` which enqueues a Retrofit call to auth endpoint (ugh). That was fine on okhttp 4.9, but on emulator with HTTP/2 multiplexing it seems to hold the connection open and cancellation doesn't free the socket until GC.

devin-sdk: That rings a bell — ordering of interceptors vs authenticator and using synchronous network requests inside authenticate() can deadlock with connection pool. Try making the refresh call use a separate OkHttpClient instance (no shared dispatcher/connectionPool). Also ensure your Authenticator does not call enqueue() on the same client.

kevin-platform: Copying a separate client fixed a similar issue for us in dedicated builds. Also check `Dispatcher.setMaxRequestsPerHost(...)` and `ConnectionPool.evictAll()` on shutdown path. We added `app.onTrimMemory()` to expire idle connections.

maria-ux: tried swapping to a dedicated refresh client and the socket count stabilizes. But curious — should we document this in the SDK onboarding? it's a footgun for people using Retrofit authenticators and coroutines.

devin-sdk: yes — we should add a note in auth docs and a sample Authenticator implementation that uses a separate client or explicit synchronous refresh that uses low-level HTTP call without sharing dispatcher. I'll draft a short blurb and include the minimal code: 
```
// avoid using the same client inside Authenticator
private val refreshClient = okHttpClient.newBuilder()
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 2 })
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(0, 1, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
  .build()

override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
  synchronized(this) { /* token refresh with refreshClient.execute() */ }
}
```

devin-sdk: also opened a small test and a fix note: PR #1427 (draft) — will add an integration test that simulates rapid cancel/rotate on API 29/30 with HTTP/2. ci-bot: can you create a flaky test alert if it regresses?

ci-bot: Created test job `devex/okhttp-cancel-leak-smoke` linked to PR #1427. It will run on emulator API 29/30. :robot_face: 

maria-ux: awesome. I'll add a short paragraph to the Android SDK quickstart about "authenticator isolation" + a small sample app change. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
